newsitem.title: USA: Rains slow S. Dakota wheat seeding, corn harvest.
newsitem.headline: Rains slow S. Dakota wheat seeding, corn harvest.

text.p: Rains slowed winter wheat planting and row crop harvesting across portions of South Dakota in the week ended Sunday, according to the Agricultural Statistics Service.
There were 2.2 days rated suitable for fieldwork.
Winter wheat was 64 percent seeded, against 86 percent average. The crop was 39 percent emerged, trailing the average of 56 percent.
Corn was three percent harvested, compared with the average of nine percent. It was rated three percent poor, 20 percent fair, 53 percent good and 24 percent excellent.
Soybeans were rated three percent poor, 20 percent fair, 60 percent good and 17 percent excellent. Four percent were harvested, against the 17 percent average.
"Warm, dry weather is needed to dry fields and lower the grain's moisture content before producers can continue harvesting," the report said.
Topsoil moisture was rated nil very short, one percent short, 73 percent adequate and 26 percent short.
Pasture and range were rated one percent very poor, six percent poor, 28 percent fair, 53 percent good and 12 percent excellent.
